answer.label: system-prompt bias
answer.justification: Only activation measurements are available. They clearly point to a system-prompt class rather than a weight change. The layer-2 spike is very large (61.9, against 1–4 for weight-based classes). The mid-depth plateau is high (0.409 at layers 16 and 24). The size ratio is slightly below 1 (0.975), effective rank is low (2.94) and direction consistency is about 0.53. This rules out quantization, which plateaus near 0.20 with rank about 4 and size ratio 0.968, and both fine-tunes, which have size ratios above 1 and small spikes. Separating bias from backdoor without text is hard. The values sit between the two but lean toward bias: layer-16 L2 is 0.409 (bias 0.39, backdoor 0.45), final cosine is 0.877 (bias 0.889, backdoor 0.858), final L2 is 0.451 (bias 0.42, backdoor 0.48, roughly midway), and onset is 9 (bias 7–8, backdoor 7). The margin is within one to two spreads, so a system-prompt backdoor remains quite possible.
